notes: The image labels the breadboard's lower half rows a-e (row a at the bottom), which matches catalogue bank 't' (rows a-e). The buzzer legs go in 15t.a (black, negative) and 18t.a (purple, positive).

A breadboard hole holds one lead. The image draws each wire end in the same column as a buzzer leg, but the two can't share a hole. I put each jumper wire in the next hole up the same column strip (15t.b and 18t.b). The electrical result is the same.
Buzzer port '1' is assumed to be the positive leg and '2' the negative leg. The catalogue does not say which is which.
The ground wire goes to the GND pin next to GPIO17 (physical pin 9). I assumed this is catalogue port GND.2, because the catalogue does not give the GND numbering.
Jumper wires are male-to-female. Port 'a' is the male end in the breadboard and port 'b' is the female end on the Pi header pin.
The image labels the header with Pico-style names (GP17), but the manual says GPIO 17 on a Raspberry Pi, so I used the raspberry-pi part.
No resistor is used, as in the manual.
